About the tune

  • Music (1863): William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868)

Metre: 8.8.8.8.8.8. Hymns on this site in the same metre: And Can It Be, Blind Bartimaeus, Day of Wrath, O Day of Mourning, Faith of Our Fathers, My Hope Is Built, O Come O Come Emmanuel.

Melody from the Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (CCEH, public domain); tune SOLID ROCK by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868). The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about Solid Rock

What is the doh of Solid Rock?

In this version, in F major, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Solid Rock start on?

It starts on s, (C in F major), a pickup before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to s,.

What words can be sung to Solid Rock?

Solid Rock is in the metre 8.8.8.8.8.8: lines of 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it, such as And Can It Be, Blind Bartimaeus, Day of Wrath, O Day of Mourning; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Solid Rock in the public domain?

Yes. William Batchelder Bradbury died in 1868; the tune was first published in 1863. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
